comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: twelve years of active trading ending in SCHD is the most honest ending this sub gets. the bit I'd push on is "models aren't supposed to beat the market": whoever closes an inefficiency gets paid for closing it, and that payment is what beating the market means.

replies.author: InvestigatorOwn2028
replies.body: Thanks for the encouragement. I just find it hard to believe that I could ever beat the market. I want to develop a model that can outperform, but I feel like I’m light years away from perfect prediction.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
nobody beats it with perfect prediction. the people who do it have a small edge, repeated many times, that still holds after fees. that's a much lower bar.

if you want a place to try a model without risking anything, Quantradin is the thing I built for that, every idea gets tested on old prices and then run with fake money. quantradin.com

replies.author: InvestigatorOwn2028
replies.body: I'm trying a manual back test for just 5 of the components over the past ten years. Do you have any suggestions for making the test empirically rigorous? The model is just a spreadsheet right now. I haven't tried to turn it into a fully functional bot. Honestly, I don't know how yet.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: write the rules down before you look at the old data: exact entry, exit, and position size, and then don't touch them. build on the first seven years and check once on the last three. and log each trade at the price you could actually have gotten that day, not the close you saw afterward.
